phoneme_focus: Stress shift in noun forms; '-tion' /ʃən/ and '-ment' /mənt/ endings

grammar_point.title: Nominalisation (verbs/adjectives → nouns) for formal register
grammar_point.en: Turn actions and qualities into noun phrases for academic register: 'prices rose' → 'the rise in prices'.
grammar_point.ar: تحويل الأفعال والصفات إلى عبارات اسمية للأسلوب الأكاديمي: 'prices rose' ← 'the rise in prices'.

Saturday.prompt: Rephrase five verb sentences as noun phrases: 'X happened' → 'the X of…'.

Sunday.prompt: Describe a trend using 'the rise/decline/expansion of…'.

Monday.prompt: Give a mini academic summary using at least four nominalised phrases.

Tuesday.prompt: Explain a cause and effect using 'the introduction of… led to…'.

Wednesday.prompt: Discuss an abstract idea (significance, complexity, reliability) formally.

Thursday.prompt: Debate a policy with a partner using nominalised, formal language.

Friday.prompt: Present a formal analytical paragraph (10-12 sentences) rich in nominalisation.

writing_prompts: Rewrite five active-verb sentences as nominalised noun phrases.
Write a formal paragraph describing a trend ('the rise/decline of…').
Turn three adjectives into abstract nouns and use them (complexity, reliability, feasibility).
Write a cause-and-effect statement using 'the introduction of… resulted in…'.
Write an academic-style summary of a topic using nominalisation.
Contrast an informal sentence with its formal, nominalised version.
Write an analytical paragraph on a social trend using at least six nominalised phrases.
